Source. After `fu_uswid_firmware_parse()` slices the inner payload, `cbor_load()` materializes the attacker-controlled coSWID bytes into a CBOR object graph. The saved allocation stack shows this decode allocating the later 5-byte text-string node that will be misused as a hash array element.

The decoded root map reaches the `FU_COSWID_TAG_PAYLOAD` entry and forwards its value into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_one_or_many()`. This payload subtree contains the malformed `FILE -> HASH` structure that later reaches the sink.
The witness encodes the top-level `PAYLOAD` value as an array, so `parse_one_or_many()` takes the array arm and extracts one payload map `value` for `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_payload()`.

Inside that payload map, the loop reaches the `FU_COSWID_TAG_FILE` entry and forwards its value toward the file parser. In the witness this file value is already a map, so `parse_one_or_many()` immediately enters `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` on that same subtree.
The file's `HASH` field passes only an outer-container check: it must be an array with at least one element. No validation here proves that every outer-array element is itself a hash tuple array.
The parser extracts the first outer `HASH` element. In the staged bytes this first element is the definite 2-item array `[1, <36-byte bytestring>]`, so it looks like a valid hash tuple.

Because that first outer element is itself an array, the parser assumes the entire outer `HASH` value is an array of hash arrays and dispatches the full outer array to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array()`. This decision is based only on element 0 and ignores the shapes of later elements.

On the next `parse_hash_array()` iteration after the valid tuple, `value` becomes the next outer `HASH` element. The first tuple's 36-byte bytestring runs through offset `0x143`, and the extracted element starts at `0x144` as CBOR text item `65 6E 2D 55 53 08`, i.e. a 5-byte text item with payload bytes `6E 2D 55 53 08`, not an array. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` receives this `value` as its `item` parameter.

Root cause and sink. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` immediately calls `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` before any `cbor_isa_array(item)` guard. Here `item` is the non-array 5-byte text item from step 8, so libcbor treats that 5-byte string allocation as array storage and AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 8` at `libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23` on address `0x602000001990`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x602000001990, 0x602000001995)`.
